summary: Unclaimed credits applied to incorrect cost center on finalized invoice for Dedicated account
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a $12,450 provisional credit (for hourly burst credits) on invoice INV-2026-03-07 was incorrectly attributed to CostCenter:OPS instead of CostCenter:AD-ML. The invoice has been finalized and posted to their accounting system, and the customer is requesting an explanation and corrective action.

Impact: Finance at BrightPulse is unable to reconcile month-end expenses across cost centers. This affects internal chargebacks for two product teams and delays their internal audit. The amount is material for the customer's internal billing (>$10k).

Environment: Dedicated account ID bp-9983 running reserved pool in us-west-2, using hybrid fallback to hosted for burst windows. Billing pipeline processed the invoice on 2026-03-07 with postbacks aggregated hourly.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer ran a cross-team batch embedding job on 2026-03-04 that spanned two cost center tags in their metadata (AD-ML and OPS).
2) During a burst window (2026-03-04 22:00-22:30 UTC) the job triggered hosted fallback and microburst credits were generated.
3) Billing postback handler received mixed postbacks; one subset had cost_center tag "AD-ML" and another subset had a legacy tag "ops" (lowercase) sent by the customer's orchestration layer.
4) Final invoice lines show the credits consolidated under CostCenter:OPS (normalized uppercase mapping) while usage lines for the same job were split.

Logs / evidence provided: Attached CSV of postbacks (postbacks_bp-9983_2026-03-04.csv), invoice PDF INV-2026-03-07.pdf, and a screenshot of customer's internal chargeback report.

Customer request: Explain root cause and provide remediation (adjust invoice lines or apply correcting credit), and confirm a fix so future postbacks are normalized consistently.
comments: 2026-03-13 - Initial customer comment (Sarah Wong, BrightPulse finance): 'We see a $12,450 credit on line 4 of INV-2026-03-07 that is labeled OPS. This credit should be applied to AD-ML. Please advise — this prevents our month-end close.'

2026-03-13 - Support (Maya Chen): 'Thanks Sarah — we have opened SUP-665432 and are triaging. Could you attach the postback export (raw JSON) if available and confirm the API keys used for the job? We'll prioritize this because the invoice is finalized.'

2026-03-13 - Customer reply (Sarah Wong): 'Attached CSV and the invoice PDF. The orchestration team reports they recently normalized tags to uppercase, but some older workers still emit lowercase "ops".'

2026-03-14 - Billing engineer (Liam O'Connor): 'Investigating — initial query shows ~3,600 postbacks for bp-9983 on 2026-03-04 and ~1,120 of them contain cost_center values "ops" (lowercase) while the rest use "AD-ML". The reconciler normalizes via exact-match mapping table which currently contains "OPS" => CostCenter:OPS and "AD-ML" => CostCenter:AD-ML, but does not canonicalize case. Filing as root-cause candidate: case-sensitive tag mapping.'

2026-03-14 - Support to customer (Maya Chen): 'We have a provisional plan: apply a correcting credit of $12,450 to CostCenter:AD-ML in your next billing cycle and backfill an off-cycle credit if you need an immediate correction. Engineering will implement a reconciler fix to case-normalize cost_center tags. Documentation will be updated. We will confirm next steps after engineering triage.'
investigation_notes:
Queries run: SELECT count(*) FROM billing.postbacks WHERE account_id='bp-9983' AND DATE(event_time)='2026-03-04' GROUP BY lower(cost_center); Results show 1120 with lower(cost_center)='ops' and 2480 with lower(cost_center)='ad-ml'. Reconciler mapping uses exact string matching: mapping table lacked lowercasing step. Correlated invoice lines: credit line id CL-8891 aggregated credits using mapping resolution logic that selected OPS bucket for lowercase 'ops' values because of a legacy alias entry 'ops' => OPS but full-route consolidation collapsed mixed-case inputs into a single canonical bucket due to alias precedence rules.

Relevant artifacts: attached postbacks CSV, invoice render, reconciler config (billing-reconciler v2.1.3).

Hypothesis: Inconsistent tag case from customer's worker fleet combined with alias precedence in the reconciliation algorithm caused credits to be grouped under OPS. This only affected credit aggregation path (not usage lines) because the credit aggregator uses a different alias resolution step for historical reasons.

Immediate risk: Customer's accounting mismatch and potential duplicate corrective actions if not handled carefully. No platform-wide financial exposure identified beyond this account so far.
resolution_notes:
Status: Pending engineering fix and customer agreement on remediation. Work items and proposed timeline:
1) Short-term remediation (executed 2026-03-14): Support applied a provisional off-cycle credit of $12,450 to CostCenter:AD-ML and issued a credit memo CM-2026-03-14-665432. Customer requested the off-cycle credit to expedite their reconciliation.
2) Engineering change (target): Implement case-normalization in billing-reconciler mapping logic and add unit test coverage. Target PR: billing-reconciler#412 (in review). Expected deploy to staging 2026-03-17, to prod 2026-03-20 after validation.
3) Post-deploy follow-up: Re-run invoice reprocessing tool for bp-9983 for the window 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-07 with corrected mapping to verify no other misattributed lines. If discrepancies remain, issue formal invoice adjustment and notify customer billing contacts.
4) Preventive: Add a monitoring alert for cost_center tag entropy (new metric: pct_unknown_alias > 0.5% over 1h) and update support KB about common customer tag normalization pitfalls.

Follow-up actions assigned: Liam O'Connor (engineering) to land PR and run reprocess job; Maya Chen (support) to coordinate credit memo and confirm with BrightPulse finance once reprocessing completes. Estimated resolution: 2026-03-20.
resolution: Pending - provisional credit applied and engineering fix in progress
